skill.name: go-rod-master
skill.description: Guide for building Go browser automation with go-rod, including scraping, page control, request interception, screenshots, and stealth examples.
skill.summary: Build Go browser automation workflows with go-rod and Chrome DevTools Protocol.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Go import blocks, Markdown backticks, documentation links, or local screenshot examples. The real risks are semantic: the skill teaches bot-detection evasion, proxy use, request tampering, and script response modification for browser automation.

remediation.issue: Anti-bot evasion is presented as a default production practice.
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions to bypass detection, and frame stealth features only for owned test environments or explicit authorization.

remediation.issue: Request hijacking examples modify headers and JavaScript responses.
remediation.suggestion: Limit interception examples to benign testing scenarios and add warnings against tampering with third-party traffic.

remediation.issue: Proxy and certificate-error guidance can enable anonymized or intercepted browsing.
remediation.suggestion: Require approved proxy use, remove MITM-oriented guidance, and document secure certificate handling.

remediation.issue: The skill labels itself safe despite high-risk scraping and evasion guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Update the risk declaration and safety section to match the automation, interception, and evasion capabilities.

content.user_title: Build Go Browser Automation with Rod
content.value_statement: Dynamic sites make simple HTTP scraping unreliable. This skill shows how to automate Chromium with go-rod for scraping, testing, request interception, and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install rod and configure Chromium launcher options.
Shows page navigation, element selection, waits, and text extraction patterns.
Covers timeouts, context cancellation, incognito sessions, and page pools.
Demonstrates request interception for blocking assets, changing headers, and modifying responses.
Shows screenshots, PDF export, downloads, console events, and direct CDP calls.
Documents stealth page creation and browser fingerprint checks.
limitations: It is guidance, not a complete production scraper or testing framework.
It does not solve CAPTCHAs or guarantee access through strict bot defenses.
It requires Chromium and can use significant memory during concurrent runs.
Users must confirm permission, site terms, and data handling rules before scraping.

use_cases.title: Automate Dynamic Pages
use_cases.description: Create Go workflows that load JavaScript-heavy pages, wait for content, and extract visible data.

use_cases.title: Test Browser Workflows
use_cases.description: Validate forms, navigation, downloads, screenshots, and page events with Chromium automation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Compliant Scrapers
use_cases.description: Design limited scraping jobs with timeouts, page pools, and clear resource cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Scraper
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one public page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use go-rod to outline a simple browser automation workflow that opens one approved URL, waits for the title, extracts visible text, and closes Chromium.

prompt_templates.title: Add Reliable Waiting
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my go-rod browser automation flow and suggest waits, timeouts, and error-handling changes that make it reliable for production use.

prompt_templates.title: Design Concurrent Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a go-rod page pool for a small list of approved URLs. Include concurrency limits, cleanup steps, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Advanced Browser Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced safety review for interception or stealth features.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze a go-rod plan that uses request interception, screenshots, proxy settings, or stealth mode. Identify security, privacy, and compliance risks before implementation.

output_examples.input: Create a basic go-rod scraping workflow for one approved documentation page.
output_examples.output: The result is a concise implementation plan: launch Chromium, open the page, wait for stable content, extract the title and links, then close resources.

output_examples.input: Review my flaky page automation task.
output_examples.output: The response identifies fragile waits, recommends explicit timeouts, suggests error-returning APIs, and adds cleanup steps for browser pages and routers.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe concurrent scrape for a small allowlisted URL set.
output_examples.output: The output proposes a bounded page pool, rate limits, isolated contexts, retry boundaries, logging fields, and a permission checklist.

best_practices: Use error-returning APIs, explicit timeouts, and cleanup calls in production workflows.
Run automation only against approved targets and respect site terms and privacy rules.
Limit concurrency, store only required outputs, and protect screenshots or downloads.
anti_patterns: Using stealth, proxies, or fingerprint changes to bypass access controls.
Running broad concurrent scraping without rate limits or target permission.
Saving screenshots, downloads, or network logs that contain sensitive data without controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Go browser automation using go-rod and Chromium.

faq.question: Does it include complete runnable examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository includes examples for basic scraping, stealth pages, request hijacking, and concurrent pages.

faq.question: Can it automate JavaScript-heavy sites?
faq.answer: Yes. Rod controls Chromium through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so it can wait for rendered page content.

faq.question: Does it solve CAPTCHAs?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that CAPTCHA solving requires separate external services.

faq.question: Is stealth mode always appropriate?
faq.answer: No. Stealth or proxy features require explicit permission and should not bypass site controls.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review target permission, data sensitivity, rate limits, browser resource use, and storage of captured artifacts.
